blocks.content: Imagine sending one segment, then waiting for its acknowledgment to fully arrive before sending the next one, and repeating this forever. On a connection with any real round trip delay at all, this would leave the sender sitting idle most of the time, wasting the vast majority of available bandwidth. Sliding window exists to fix exactly this.
This topic builds directly on both sequence numbers and acknowledgments, the previous two topics in this module, and puts the receive window from the flow control topic into actual mechanical motion.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784014698056-293507992.png
blocks.alt: Stop and wait leaves the sender idle most of the time; sliding window keeps multiple segments in flight to stay busy

blocks.content: 1. The Core Idea: Multiple Segments Outstanding at Once
blocks.text: 1. The Core Idea: Multiple Segments Outstanding at Once

blocks.content: Rather than sending one segment and waiting, the sender is allowed to have MULTIPLE segments outstanding, sent but not yet acknowledged, at the same time, up to a certain limit called the window size. This window size is exactly the receive window from the flow control topic, being put into actual mechanical action here.

blocks.title: One mechanism, two names
blocks.content: Flow control introduced the receive window as a number the receiver advertises. Sliding window is the sender side mechanism that actually uses that number to decide how much can be safely in flight at once. Same underlying concept, seen from two angles.
2. The Window as a Moving Frame Over the Data Stream
blocks.text: 2. The Window as a Moving Frame Over the Data Stream

blocks.content: Picture the byte stream as a long line. The window is a frame covering some contiguous range of it. Everything to the left of the window has already been sent and acknowledged. Everything inside the window can be sent right now. Everything to the right of the window cannot be sent yet at all.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784014700002-1125.png
blocks.alt: The window is a moving frame: acknowledged data to the left, sendable data inside it, not yet allowed data to the right

blocks.content: As acknowledgments arrive confirming bytes at the left edge, the window slides forward, allowing new bytes at the right edge to now be sent.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784014701501-747092480.png
blocks.alt: As acknowledgments confirm data at the left edge, the entire window slides forward, opening up new bytes on the right

blocks.content: 3. A Full Worked Example

A window size of 3000 bytes starting at byte 1000, so bytes 1000 through 3999 can be sent immediately. Once an acknowledgment arrives confirming bytes up through 1999, tying back to the cumulative confirmation from the acknowledgments topic, the window slides forward, now covering bytes 2000 through 4999, newly allowing bytes 4000 through 4999 to be sent that could not be sent before.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784014703052-129627778.png
blocks.alt: A window of size 3000 slides forward by exactly the amount confirmed, opening new bytes for sending

4. A Bigger Window Is Not Unlimited
blocks.text: 4. A Bigger Window Is Not Unlimited

blocks.content: A larger window lets more data be in flight at once, better using available bandwidth especially on high latency connections. But the window size is fundamentally capped by whatever the receiver has said it can actually handle, tying back precisely to the flow control topic receive window advertisement. Sending more than the receiver can hold would just overwhelm it.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784014704738-475452650.png
blocks.alt: The window size is always capped by the receiver own advertised capacity, straight from the flow control topic

blocks.content: 5. The Bandwidth Delay Product

The ideal window size for fully using a connection available bandwidth is related to the round trip time and the available bandwidth together. A connection with high bandwidth AND high latency, a satellite link is the classic example, actually needs a LARGER window to avoid leaving the pipe underused, since there is more round trip time during which multiple segments worth of data could otherwise be sitting in flight.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784014706625-781103566.png
blocks.alt: A high bandwidth, high latency link needs a larger window to actually keep the pipe full, not a smaller one

blocks.title: Why this matters in practice
blocks.content: A window sized for a fast local network can badly underuse a long distance, high latency link, even if that link technically has plenty of bandwidth. Matching window size to the actual round trip time genuinely matters.
6. Stop and Wait Versus Sliding Window, With Real Numbers
blocks.text: 6. Stop and Wait Versus Sliding Window, With Real Numbers

blocks.content: With a 100 millisecond round trip time, stop and wait can only send one segment per round trip. Sliding window, with a large enough window, can keep multiple segments continuously in flight, achieving dramatically higher effective throughput on the exact same physical link.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784014708498-897960229.png
blocks.alt: On the same link with the same round trip time, sliding window achieves dramatically higher effective throughput than stop and wait

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Segments in flight","Typical throughput"],"rows":[["Stop and wait","One at a time","Limited by round trip time, often quite low"],["Sliding window","Many at once, up to the window size","Much closer to the link true available bandwidth"]]}
7. An Assembly Line Analogy

An assembly line does not wait for one finished item to be fully inspected before starting the next one, several items are in progress at various stages simultaneously. The window is exactly how many items can be in progress at once before you have to pause and wait for confirmation on the earliest ones.
https://algorithmxlr8-assets-images.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/hld-content-images/1784014711064-878859849.png
blocks.alt: An assembly line keeps several items in progress at once, pausing only once too many are in flight simultaneously

blocks.content: 8. Common Mistakes and Key Takeaways

["Assuming sliding window means sending unlimited data all at once with no limit at all, when it is specifically bounded by the receiver advertised window size.","Confusing the window sliding forward with the window simply growing bigger, sliding means the SAME size frame moves forward as old data gets acknowledged, not that it necessarily expands.","Sliding window lets multiple segments be outstanding at once, dramatically improving throughput over stop and wait.","The window slides forward exactly as much as gets acknowledged, no more.","Window size is capped by the receiver, straight from the flow control topic.","High latency, high bandwidth links need a larger window to stay fully utilized."]
items: Assuming sliding window means sending unlimited data all at once with no limit at all, when it is specifically bounded by the receiver advertised window size.
Confusing the window sliding forward with the window simply growing bigger, sliding means the SAME size frame moves forward as old data gets acknowledged, not that it necessarily expands.
Sliding window lets multiple segments be outstanding at once, dramatically improving throughput over stop and wait.
The window slides forward exactly as much as gets acknowledged, no more.
Window size is capped by the receiver, straight from the flow control topic.
High latency, high bandwidth links need a larger window to stay fully utilized.
